chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 414 — Li Huowang Meets the Supervisor: A Trap Wrapped in a Promise
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang's audience with the Supervisor goes wrong. Instead of hunting the Zuowandao, he's ordered to betray Zhuge Yuan—and a death notice reminds him of the cost of refusal.
og_description: A quiet office, a warm stove, and a cold ultimatum. Li Huowang learns that the Supervisory Heavenly Office plays a game far older and deadlier than any sect.
twitter_description: Li Huowang walks into a trap dressed as a promotion. Betray his friend or lose his head? The Supervisor doesn’t leave room for a third choice.

lore_anchors.definition: A famous Chinese oolong tea (“Big Red Robe”), often served to honored guests or in formal settings; the Supervisor’s casual brewing implies both refinement and a deliberate show of control.
A divinatory calendar system used in traditional Chinese chronomancy; in this novel, it is portrayed as a powerful artifact that Zhuge Yuan possesses, hinting at fate-manipulation abilities.
In imperial Chinese bureaucracy, red ink (cinnabar) was used for official markings; a vermillion circle or stamp on a document could signify approval, final judgment, or a death sentence.
A bureaucratic title within the Supervisory Heavenly Office; Feng Erniu, the fat eunuch, held this post before his sudden death, which Li Huowang discovers was treated as routine paperwork.
Li Huowang’s alias while infiltrating the Office, meaning “Ear Nine”; a transparent false identity that the Office likely sees through but tolerates for their own purposes.
